checklist.evidence: AgyBuilder.run preserves the exact keyword-only injected Builder signature.

blocking_findings.contract_source: Astra execution-isolation invariant, Step 2 execution contract, and Step 7 requirement 2
blocking_findings.exact_requirement: Every production AGY dispatch must execute through the approved filesystem isolation boundary, must not inherit writable workspace/configuration overrides, and must give the Builder no Git or trusted-state authority.
blocking_findings.concrete_evidence: AgyBuilder.run builds argv beginning with the host agy executable and calls run_builder_process directly with cwd=candidate and env=os.environ.copy(). The Step 6 Job Object/process-group supervisor controls lifecycle but provides no filesystem isolation. No Windows Sandbox or equivalent audited execution boundary is invoked, inherited workspace/configuration overrides are not removed, and FactoryEngine now selects this path by default.
blocking_findings.observed_state: Production AGY executes directly on the host with permission skipping and can reach candidate Git metadata, source/trusted paths, user configuration, credentials, and unrelated host paths permitted to the user account.
blocking_findings.expected_state: The exact production invocation must run inside the Step 2-approved isolation boundary with only the disposable candidate writable, Git/source/trusted-state and unrelated host paths inaccessible, and sanitized configuration/workspace discovery.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks_current_step: Step 7 activates an unrestricted permission-skipping Builder as the production default, concretely regressing candidate isolation and no-Builder-Git invariants.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Route AgyBuilder.run through the audited production isolation launcher while retaining the Step 6 bounded supervisor and exact inner AGY argv; sanitize prohibited inherited overrides and add a production-path fixture proving source, Git metadata, trusted state, and unrelated paths cannot be written.

blocking_findings.contract_source: Astra Step 7 pre-dispatch contract and Step 7 requirement 3
blocking_findings.exact_requirement: Validate the canonical disposable candidate cwd and bind the complete candidate baseline before dispatch.
blocking_findings.concrete_evidence: _canonical_builder_worktree only requires candidate.is_dir(), candidate != source, and run_root not beneath candidate. It does not prove that candidate is the factory-created disposable worktree or reject a candidate that contains the source/trusted roots. The attempt manifest records baseline_head plus snapshots only for allowed_files, omitting staged, unstaged, untracked, ignored, and out-of-scope baseline state.
blocking_findings.observed_state: An arbitrary Git directory, including an ancestor containing protected paths, can satisfy validation, and the recorded baseline cannot distinguish pre-existing or concurrent candidate state outside allowed_files.
blocking_findings.expected_state: Candidate provenance and canonical identity must be validated against the run's authorized disposable worktree; protected roots must be disjoint, and the attempt must bind an unambiguous whole-candidate baseline identity appropriate to this step.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks_current_step: The pre-dispatch safety decision and retained evidence are not bound to the candidate actually authorized for editing.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Validate candidate identity/provenance and disjointness from source, run-state, review, and Git-protected roots; record a canonical complete baseline identity before dispatch; add ancestor, unrelated-repository, dirty-index, untracked, and out-of-scope baseline tests.

blocking_findings.contract_source: Astra Step 7 stream requirements and Step 7 requirement 4
blocking_findings.exact_requirement: Require a consistent fresh conversation for every invocation and the audited stream structure, including step updates.
blocking_findings.concrete_evidence: Conversation IDs are added to _conversation_ids only after full success. ERROR results raise inside parse_agy_event_stream, and wrong-model/cwd failures occur before insertion, so a later invocation may reuse the failed attempt's conversation ID and be accepted. The set is also process-local. Additionally, init followed directly by a SUCCESS result with num_turns greater than zero is accepted without any step_update record.
blocking_findings.observed_state: Freshness is checked only against successful calls in the current AgyBuilder instance, and an incomplete event sequence can pass.
blocking_findings.expected_state: Every observed init identity, including failed attempts, must be durably bound to its unique attempt and rejected on reuse; the parser must enforce the audited event sequence.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks_current_step: Stale conversation state or fabricated incomplete protocol evidence can be accepted as a fresh successful Builder completion.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Persist or otherwise durably reserve each init conversation identity before terminal acceptance, consult prior attempt evidence, require the audited step-update sequence, and test reuse after ERROR, model/cwd failure, and a new builder instance.

blocking_findings.contract_source: Astra Step 7 structured-failure contract and Step 7 requirement 5
blocking_findings.exact_requirement: All spawn, timeout, cancellation, protocol, runtime, model, identity, output, and isolation failures must become stable BuilderFailure codes with retained evidence.
blocking_findings.concrete_evidence: _builder_process_failure_code has no path returning agy_isolation_failed, so Job Object/process-group creation, assignment, quiescence, or closure failures fall through to agy_runtime_error. Attempt-directory creation can raise a raw OSError; final atomic_json persistence after a successful process can also raise an unstructured exception. Initial artifact failures are mislabeled agy_spawn_failed even though no spawn occurred, and _builder_attempt_failure may return an evidence_path after swallowing failure to create that file.
blocking_findings.observed_state: Several required failure classes are misclassified or escape BuilderFailure, and evidence_path can identify nonexistent evidence.
blocking_findings.expected_state: Supervisor causes and artifact failures must deterministically map to the appropriate stable code, remain non-resumable, and report only verified retained evidence.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks_current_step: Failure state drives safe stopping and later resume behavior; ambiguous or false failure evidence affects execution correctness.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Use typed supervisor failure causes or exact structured mapping, map process-boundary failures to agy_isolation_failed, wrap all attempt creation/finalization failures in BuilderFailure, and expose evidence_path only after verified persistence.

blocking_findings.contract_source: Step 7 requirement 6 and predecessor HOH memory/provenance invariant touched by the production-default switch
blocking_findings.exact_requirement: Keep the production default and existing engine behavior aligned with the Step 7 adapter and preserve valid evidence provenance.
blocking_findings.concrete_evidence: AgyBuilder writes evidence under builder_attempts/<label>-<uuid>/, but unchanged engine routes still record artifacts such as builder_initial.log, builder_debug_<n>.log, and builder_review_rework_<n>.log, which AgyBuilder never creates. The production initial prompt still tells AGY that Aider is the Lean Builder.
blocking_findings.observed_state: Successful production events reference nonexistent legacy artifacts and send backend-inaccurate instructions immediately after FactoryEngine switches its default to AgyBuilder.
blocking_findings.expected_state: Every production route must record the actual attempt artifact path and use backend-correct instructions, or the default switch must remain blocked until that integration is valid.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks_current_step: The default switch creates false machine-verifiable provenance and misaligns runtime behavior with the reviewed adapter.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Update current engine artifact references and Builder wording for AgyBuilder, verify each referenced artifact exists, and add a production-default engine test covering initial and repair-route evidence.

blocking_findings.contract_source: Astra per-step review protocol and Step 7 requirement 6
blocking_findings.exact_requirement: Provide tests for every required negative class, zero-exit error/timeout, partial-edit failure, and an invariant-to-test mapping with exact verification exit codes and limitations.
blocking_findings.concrete_evidence: The added Step 7 tests exercise valid argv, parser malformed/missing/duplicate/error cases, wrong model/cwd, one in-memory stale ID, nonzero exit, and one synthetic timeout exception. They do not exercise AgyBuilder mappings for spawn, cancellation, output exhaustion/malformed UTF-8, identity change, process-boundary isolation failure, zero-exit timeout stderr, or partial candidate edits followed by protocol/runtime failure. The fixture file only lists case names. The packet supplies test counts but no explicit command exit code, invariant-to-test mapping, or known-limitations/skipped-checks/release-blockers section.
blocking_findings.observed_state: Passing 95 tests does not establish the explicitly required Step 7 negative-path contract, and required review evidence is incomplete.
blocking_findings.expected_state: Concrete executable tests must cover each listed failure through AgyBuilder.run, and the refreshed packet must map every Step 7 invariant to those tests with exact commands, exit codes, counts, limitations, skips, and blockers.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks_current_step: Required safety and completion behavior remains unproven for the reviewed candidate.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Add the missing AgyBuilder integration tests, replace metadata-only negative-case names with executable fixtures, rerun the affected suite, and submit a complete protocol-valid evidence packet.
